title: Long-context & context-distillation notes - Trent Z.
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal reference: collection of papers, rough experiments, and whiteboard ideas around making long context windows usable in production (>= 65k tokens).
- Focus: tradeoffs between chunking/stitching, context distillation (compressing context into compact state), and KV-cache eviction strategies for serving.

Papers / posts skimmed (notes):
1) "Context Distillation for Long-Range Reasoning" (arXiv 2026) - sketch
   - idea: run expensive model on full document offline, distill into small adapter vectors that are inserted in front of prompt at serve-time.
   - method: hierarchical summarization -> projector network -> fixed-size summary tokens that become soft prompts.
   - pros: constant-size insertion, cheap at inference. cons: loses token-level grounding; failure modes on referential ambiguity.
   - note: could combine with sparse retrieval to rehydrate details on low-confidence queries.

2) "KV-Cache Eviction w/ Relevance Score" (workshop paper, 2025)
   - store KV entries for sliding window; evict by recency*relevance rather than pure LRU.
   - compute cheap relevance via small bi-encoder comparing active prompt vs past segments.
   - tradeoff: additional compute for scoring vs reduced model degradation.

3) "Chunk-then-stitch: deterministic output merging" (blog + code repo)
   - generate on overlapping chunks, then deterministic merge with anchor tokens and reconciliation rules.
   - recommended when output is largely extractive (summarization, Q&A). Not great for creative generation.

4) Sparse attention locality + global tokens (NeurIPS '25 followups)
   - local windows with fixed set of global tokens; global tokens can be used as index positions for topic-level info.
   - implementation note: in many open models, enabling globals requires custom kernels; check Redwood runtime kernel selection paths.

Quick mental model / tradeoffs:
- Full-context model (no compression): best fidelity, worst cost and latency.
- Chunking + stitch: reduces immediate memory, but needs careful merge logic; latency depends on chunk concurrency.
- Distillation to adapter tokens: constant-size prefix, best for tail latency but risks hallucination if the distiller mis-encodes pointers.
- Retriever + on-demand rehydration: hybrid; store dense vectors per chunk and re-fetch only top-K when query arrives.

Ideas to try (experiments I can run on Redwood Dedicated dev pool):
- A: Small distillation prototype
  - pipeline: full model (gpt-like, 32k context) -> greedy extractive passage selection -> projector MLP to 128-d vector -> map to 64 soft prompt tokens
  - eval: use held-out long docs (legal docs) and run targeted QA; measure exact match + calibration of hallucination (precision of answers).
  - metric targets: match baseline F1 within 5% while reducing per-request token cost by >40%.

- B: KV-eviction by relevance score
  - implement small bi-encoder (mini-bert) to compute similarity between live prompt and cached chunks; evict entries where recency*sim < threshold
  - AB test vs LRU on synthetic workloads (news stream with topic drift) measuring perplexity and token-level coherence.

- C: Chunk-stitch rules library
  - create set of deterministic merge heuristics: prefer anchor sentences, avoid duplicate lines, preserve citations.
  - instrument with failure taxonomy: misaligned referents, broken coreference, time inconsistency.

Practical constraints & Redwood considerations:
- Serving runtime: need to verify kernel support for global tokens and adapted prompt injection. Check infra/serving-runtime/notes for kernel compatibility (ticket: SRV-882).
- Caching: ensure cache keys are stable across model variants/quantization; hashed KV entries must include model-id and quantization flags.
- Rollouts: test distillation prefix as a model variant with canary and automatic fallback to full-context model on high-uncertainty queries. Use console rollouts features.

Evaluation plan / metrics:
- Fidelity: exact match / F1 on Q&A pairs; ROUGE for summarization.
- Hallucination rate: fraction of answers asserting unverifiable claims (manual label sample).
- Latency: p50/p95 end-to-end.
- Cost: tokens served + model compute time.
- Regression detection: tie into Redwood Optimize-quality monitors to trigger alerts if distillation variant diverges.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How stable are distillation vectors across document edits? Do we need versioned adapters?
- What's the right dimensionality vs token-length tradeoff for soft-prefixes? empirical sweep needed.
- How to do provenance: if answer cites a distilled vector, how to map back to source chunk reliably?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- TODO: sketch simple distillation training loop (pseudocode) and share with Aisha.
- TODO: search codebase for existing projector modules (likely in applied-ml repo).
- TODO: spin up small Dedicated test (1xA10) and run initial prototyping. File infra ticket if needed.

- Serve-time prompt template: "[DISTIL-TOKENS] 
User: {question}
Assistant:"

End notes:
